blocks.h: Chain detective: three made-up practice chains

blocks.text: These chains are invented for practice only; they are not real hadith. Each has a teaching at the end, which is not shown.

questions.q: Chain 1: Narrator A (honest, excellent memory) heard it from Narrator B (honest, excellent memory), who heard it from a Companion. Each met the one before. Connected? 'Adalah and dabt? Reliable?
questions.a: Connected; all have 'adalah and dabt: reliable.

questions.q: Chain 2: Narrator C (honest, excellent memory) reports from Narrator D, but D died before C was born. D heard it from a Companion. Connected? Reliable?
questions.a: Not connected (a gap between C and D): not reliable.

questions.q: Chain 3: Narrator E (honest, but known to forget and mix up reports) heard it from Narrator F (honest, excellent memory), who heard it from a Companion. Connected? Reliable?
questions.a: Connected, but E lacks dabt (accuracy): not reliable.

keywords.def: the chain of narrators who passed a hadith on
the actual words of the hadith
a person who passes on a hadith
uprightness: the narrator is honest and pious
precision: the narrator remembers or writes accurately

questions.q: Label the isnad and matn: 'Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: the prayer in congregation is better than prayer alone by twenty-seven degrees.'
questions.a: Isnad: Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar. Matn: 'the prayer in congregation is better than prayer alone by twenty-seven degrees.' (Bukhari and Muslim)

questions.q: Which ayah tells believers to verify news?
Chain detective (pupil PDF): three made-up practice chains. For each, say if it is connected and if each narrator has 'adalah and dabt, then decide 'reliable' or 'not reliable'.
questions.a: Chain A: connected, all reliable: reliable. Chain B: two narrators who never met: broken, not reliable. Chain C: one narrator known for lying: not reliable.

questions.q: Extend: explain Ibn al-Mubarak's words 'the isnad is part of the religion'.
questions.a: Without chains anyone could invent sayings; the chain protects the religion from lies.

questions.q: Stretch: how can you apply isnad thinking to a message forwarded on a phone?
questions.a: Ask who first said it, whether they are reliable, and whether there is a real source before sharing (49:6).

questions.q: A narrator is honest but often forgets and mixes up words. What is the problem?
questions.a: A) Weak dabt (accuracy). Honesty ('adalah) is fine; accuracy (dabt) is weak. Both are needed. The length of the matn is not the issue.

questions.q: Think again: how do you decide whether to believe 'someone said that someone said'?
questions.a: Check every person in the chain for honesty and accuracy and that the chain is connected.
